prompt:
3D highly rendered animation, soft 3D CGI look. Exactly four characters: Barnaby, Hazel, Anne and Baba. Only one Barnaby is in the frame. Subtitle-free, no logo, no watermark.

REFERENCES: @Image 1 gives Barnaby's head, antlers and colours and @Image 7 gives his full body in profile facing right; @Image 2 gives Hazel; @Image 3 gives Baba and @Image 4 gives Anne, both full body; @Image 5 is the brass bell on its pole; @Image 6 is the location. Every Barnaby reference gives identity only, never size or crop: Barnaby stays at about 42 to 50 percent of the frame height, full antlers inside the frame with clear headroom and his hooves inside the frame.

CHARACTERS: Barnaby: chubby moose upright on his two hind legs like a person, red knit sweater with ribbed cuffs; antlers dark chocolate-brown, slightly darker than his fur, about 1.8 times his head width, short round prongs; giant round matte anthracite nose about half as wide as his face, short thick caramel-brown muzzle ending right behind the nose, big round amber-copper eyes, thick brown brows. Hazel: tiny chibi chipmunk, round head about 45 percent of her body, one dark chocolate forehead stripe, flat mint scarf, bushy S-curved tail that stays a big bushy S-curve the whole time, plump cream cheeks, two very big glossy solid black eyes. Baba: large moose father upright like a person, dark chestnut fur with grey grizzle, thick dark brows, half-closed eyelids over amber eyes, grey beard, round gold-rimmed glasses, plain forest-green knit sweater with a round ribbed collar; symmetric dark chocolate velvet antlers about 2.1 times his head width, four short thick round-tipped prongs per side; blunt face-coloured muzzle, giant round matte anthracite nose. Anne: moose mother upright like a person, no antlers, smooth round head, big round ears, dark chocolate-brown fur with a cream belly, amber irises, thick mustard-yellow knit shawl without fringe tied at her chest; blunt face-coloured muzzle, giant round matte anthracite nose. FORBIDDEN: any tail, tuft or tail-like bump on Barnaby; a small or shiny nose on Barnaby; Baba's antlers on Barnaby; white eye-whites on Hazel; antlers or buds on Anne; a patterned sweater on Baba; human fingers on any character; a second Barnaby; a fifth character.

LIGHT: silver full moon gives a thin cool rim light from the upper back; four paper lanterns give one soft, even, constant golden light that warms the faces. Barnaby's fur stays warm caramel-brown and his sweater deep red, Baba's sweater forest green, Anne's shawl mustard-yellow; the night is deep blue, never black.

SUBJECT & ACTION: Barnaby stands at the left of the picture in front of the long table in a three-quarter view facing the picture-right, Hazel on his shoulder on the left side of the picture with one small smooth capless hazelnut clasped to her chest, a red maple leaf already stuck to the red sleeve of his near arm with an amber syrup smear, already there from the very first moment. Anne stands in front of the table in the middle, looking warmly up at Barnaby. Baba stands in front of the table at its right end by the bell pole, his forehoof resting against the short braided cord. Nobody sits.
Seconds 0 to 1.4: the three stand and smile, Anne's eyes on Barnaby, Barnaby's eyes on the table, his ears up.
At second 1.4 Anne turns her face to Baba and gives him one small clear nod: the table is full at last. Baba's eyes are on Anne.
At about second 2.2 Baba says low, his lips moving to the words, 'Hm.' and bows his head once, and at about second 2.8 he pulls the cord down with his forehoof in one firm tug; the brass bell swings with one loud ding, dong while the four paper lanterns stay perfectly still on their rope; Barnaby's, Hazel's and Anne's eyes go to the bell.
At about second 4.4 Baba, a small proud grin on his face and his eyes on his own hooves, steps right foot, left foot, right foot and stops, three small neat steps in the leaves; Barnaby's eyes are on Baba's hooves. At about seconds 5.6, 6.0 and 6.4 Barnaby copies the same rhythm with three soft taps of his hind hoof, standing in place, his ears bouncing; Anne smiles warmly at the two of them. From about second 7.0 all three hold their smiles. Barnaby's antlers stay on his head the whole time. He keeps his back straight and tall and never drops onto four legs.

SCENE: four round white paper lanterns hang still on one twine rope above the table, from the top of the tall wooden bell pole on the right to the maples on the left; a long wooden table with a golden pie, a bowl of cranberries, two corn cobs and a loaf of bread, with round tree-stump stools around it, already there from the very first moment; a brass bell on a bracket on the bell pole at the right end of the table with one short braided cord hanging straight down; a moonlit meadow of red and burgundy maples and fallen red leaves, a deep blue sky, no snow.

CAMERA: a steady medium wide shot of all three standing, whole figures including their hooves inside the frame with open grass below the hooves, single continuous take from second 0 to 8.0, no cut. One slow smooth push-in from second 0 to second 4.4, then the camera holds: Barnaby grows from about 42 to at most 50 percent of the frame height and stays there. Barnaby's full antlers stay inside the frame with clear headroom above them the whole shot (and every other character's antlers too), at least 25 percent of the frame height above the tallest antlers.

SOUND: only natural on-set sounds: a dry night breeze, one soft brass bell ding, dong at about second 2.8, soft hoof steps in dry leaves at 4.4 to 5.0, three soft hoof taps at 5.6, 6.0 and 6.4, a faint fabric rustle, each word heard once, Barnaby warm young male voice, Hazel tiny bright girl voice, Anne warm motherly voice, Baba warm low father voice, one line at a time.
